# requires: transfer
#
# The confused deputy at the sink field, one spelling past the containment that
# closed the relative case.
#
# A record on a store several machines can write names an ABSOLUTE sink -- on a
# NAS, /etc/cron.d/<name>. Lexical containment never saw it: an absolute path is
# never joined onto the store root, so it climbs out of nothing. The foreign-path
# rule refuses only the OTHER platform's spelling, so a path in the fetching
# machine's own convention passes every check and is written with that machine's
# authority, at a destination a record somebody else wrote chose. The drop folder
# already refuses this on its own input; the record door -- the one the runner
# actually uses -- did not.
#
# A runner over a shared store refuses it (step 2), the bytes never land, and the
# job is left adoptable rather than failed (step 3): the record is valid on the
# machine whose filesystem the path names, so this is a machine's policy and not
# a fault of the record. The driver spells the absolute path in the host's own
# convention, because which spelling is native depends on the host and the
# behaviour under test is the same on both.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=file sink=abs
runshared A alpha
state A

# expect 1: ok state=pending
# expect 2: transfer-failed state=pending [DL-R30]
# expect 2: done=0 err=set [DL-E1]
# expect 3: ok state=pending
